items.detail: A psychological thriller directed by Alfred Hitchcock that follows two young men who commit a murder and then host a dinner party with the victim's body hidden in plain sight. The film is particularly valuable for students in film studies, communication, psychology, philosophy, criminal justice, and theater because of its innovative long-take cinematography, exploration of morality and intellectual arrogance, and its adaptation of a stage play to the screen. All film screenings are free in E109. The 3:00 PM screening is sensory-friendly, with dim (not dark) lighting, reduced volume, and open captions. The 6:00 PM screening offers a full cinema experience, including free popcorn.
items.title: Rope

items.detail: A coming-of-age drama directed by Cameron Crowe that follows a teenage aspiring journalist who is given the opportunity to tour with a rising rock band while writing for Rolling Stone in the 1970s. The film is especially valuable for students in journalism, mass communication, media studies, music industry studies, sociology, and history because it explores ethical reporting, celebrity culture, youth identity, and the relationship between the media and popular music. All film screenings are free in E109. The 3:00 PM screening is sensory-friendly, with dim (not dark) lighting, reduced volume, and open captions. The 6:00 PM screening offers a full cinema experience, including free popcorn.
items.title: Almost Famous

items.detail: A science-fiction adventure directed by Luc Besson that follows a futuristic taxi driver who becomes responsible for protecting a mysterious woman whose existence is key to saving humanity from an ancient cosmic threat. The film is particularly valuable for students in film studies, communication, media studies, design, fashion, visual arts, and cultural studies because of its groundbreaking visual world-building, distinctive production design, use of satire, and exploration of technology, consumer culture, and global media. All film screenings are free in E109. The 3 p.m. screening is sensory-friendly, with dim (not dark) lighting, reduced volume, and open captions. The 6 p.m. screening offers a full cinema experience, including free popcorn.
items.title: The Fifth Element

items.detail: A DOLL'S HOUSE by Henrik Ibsen Adapted by Amy Herzog Ibsen’s celebrated play thrust drama firmly into the modern age when it premiered in 1879. Now, nearly 150 years later, acclaimed playwright Amy Herzog makes freshly relevant a story that shocked audiences and brought forth a new era of theatre. This engaging one-act adaptation of Henrik Ibsen’s classic breathes new life into the captivating tale of Nora Helmer, a spirited young woman completely devoted to her husband, Torvald. Yet, beneath the surface, not everything is as it seems: when Nora makes a bold move to safeguard her husband, she inadvertently places them both in danger, challenging the foundations of their marriage. This revelation compels them to reflect on their relationship and confront the question of how deeply they truly understand one another. Director Kevin Long: Why stage this play now? More than ever in today’s political climate, women’s rights are under increasing scrutiny and attack. This play reminds us that women are not defined solely by their roles as wives or mothers, but first and foremost as human beings deserving of autonomy, dignity, and equality. It is both striking and sobering that nearly 150 years after the play was written, these conversations remain urgently relevant today. Coffee with the Director & Dramaturg Join us Sundays at 1:00 p.m. for Coffee with the Director & Dramaturg. Director Kevin Long and Dramaturg Mary T. Christel will explore the historical context of A Doll's House, discuss the creative process behind Harper Ensemble Theatre Company's production, and examine the play's enduring relevance in today's world. Enjoy an engaging, thought-provoking conversation before the performance.
